findings.finding: doctor.py is exclusively a blocking-LINK-edge auditor: `scan`, `classify_edge`, `repair_finding`, and `run_repair` all operate on link findings (_KIND_ANCESTOR / _KIND_MIS_ESCALATED / _KIND_UNREADABLE), and doctor's finding source is `_blocking_edges` via `reduce_all_tickets` — it has no ORPHAN_EVENT finding source (that check lives in fsck_scan.py `_check_snapshot`). Routing ORPHAN_EVENT repair through `rebar doctor --repair` is therefore introduction of an entirely new finding class + new scan source + new repair kind in doctor.py — a CREATION (new behavior) hunk the plan does not classify or scope as such.

scenarios: Implementing --repair ORPHAN_EVENT in doctor requires a new scan feeding run_repair, which currently iterates only link findings

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an acceptance criterion asserting the ticket's persisted state AFTER a failed/rolled-back doctor --repair re-fold: the orphan source remains active (not stranded as *.retired), the ticket is interpreted identically to pre-repair, and fsck still reports the same ORPHAN_EVENT (no new SNAPSHOT_INCONSISTENT) — not merely that the backup ref was restored.

findings.finding: The plan changes how existing persisted records are interpreted (a previously-invisible orphan event becomes folded) and rewrites records in place (absorbing re-fold writes a new snapshot and retires the orphan source), but only asserts that a backup ref is taken 'before mutation' — it does not assert on the persisted STATE after a back-out. A restore-the-ref rollback can report success while leaving the ticket incorrectly interpreted or the orphan source stranded as *.retired (its effect living only in a discarded snapshot).
